pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered as a screen tour of the Skool library rather than as a philosophy — 'you've got literally absolutely every single kettlebell exercise you will ever do, full tutorials of all of it' plus the mobility routines. The prospect engaged practically and asked four consecutive mechanics questions: how many times a week, how long the sessions are, whether he could scale a pull-up he currently cannot complete, and what equipment is needed. Interested in the contents, never sold on the method.

The nutrition philosophy was never delivered. It appeared once, as a line item in the app tour, and the mismatch with the prospect was raised and dismissed in the same breath: 'you then have our nutrition protocol as well, now you're vegetarian, we do eat a lot of meat, but vegetarian's all good, you can still go through all this and understand it, which is going be helpful for you.' The prospect gave no reaction. Notable because the rep had already spent several minutes mapping this prospect's vegetarian diet in detail.

Presented only as the thing he would be giving up by choosing the cheaper tier: 'with the coaching it's everything's completely tailored and then you have 24/7 support from Trevor. The difference is that this is Trevor's brain written down into programs... and then you're not paying for his time. You're paying for the information.' The prospect accepted the trade without hesitation — 'Yeah, yeah' — despite having described a ten-month collapse in consistency that accountability is the direct answer to.

anchors.raw: we do also have a school community as well, um, which is more self-guided rather than complete one-on-one. Uh, and that's about 150 pounds a month.
anchors.note: The most consequential anchor in the batch, and the company created it against itself. £150 a month, rolling with no commitment, was placed beside £4,400 for six months in the same sentence, before any budget discovery and before any objection. The rep then widened the apparent gap by misstating the coaching as £880 a month rather than £733. The prospect chose the cheap tier immediately and the coaching was never mentioned again.

anchors.raw: I came across Trevor's Instagram page and I tried a few of the kettlebell exercises. It's quite like, can you do a hundred of these? It's quite an exciting opportunity to be like, okay, cool, let me do it. And it was something that felt quite helpful.
anchors.note: The prospect arrived already getting value from the free content and had independently started training again a week before the call. His demonstrated willingness is to self-serve, which is precisely what the £150 tier sells him — and it is the same pattern as the documented 'a cheaper alternative already worked' script gap.

anchors.raw: because I was rowing for like three years straight, so a lot of it would be like, sort of a week would be three times on the water, twice on the ERG machine
anchors.note: He sustained a seven-session training week for three years inside a club structure without paying for personal coaching. His evidence about himself is that structure and access, not coaching, are what he needs — which makes the accountability pillar the one that had to be sold here, and it was the one presented as optional.

unmet_demand.want: Nutrition guidance that works for a lifelong vegetarian
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's nutrition protocol is explicitly meat-centred. The rep acknowledged the conflict and moved past it in one sentence — 'we do eat a lot of meat, but vegetarian's all good, you can still go through all this and understand it, which is going be helpful for you, help you pack on a little bit more' — without describing any vegetarian adaptation, protein strategy or alternative protocol. The prospect had just described his protein sources in detail, so the mismatch was fully visible.

unmet_demand.want: Structure and rhythm to replace what he lost when he stopped rowing — 'then I didn't have, like, a set pattern'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The product he was steered toward is self-guided, monthly rolling, with no commitment period and no coach oversight. His own account is that he trains consistently inside an external structure and stops without one, so the tier presented answers his content gap rather than his adherence gap. The coaching that does address it was named and then abandoned.
